info.title: Laminus — OrcaSlicer Sidecar API
info.description:
Headless 3D model slicing via OrcaSlicer CLI running inside a Docker container. Laminus is a sidecar service used by Themis; it is not intended to be called directly by end-users in normal operation.

## Typical agent workflow

1. **`GET /api/v1/health`** — wait until `catalog_loaded: true` before making any other calls.
2. **`GET /api/v1/profiles`** — discover machine / process / filament UUIDs for your printer and material. Filter by `manufacturer`, `model`, and `nozzle` to narrow results.
3. **`POST /api/v1/jobs`** — upload the model (`.3mf` or `.stl`) with the resolved UUIDs. The response contains a `job_id`.
4. **`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`** — poll every 2–5 s until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.
5. **`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/artifact`** — retrieve the GCode (or `.3mf` when `export_3mf` was requested). Downloading evicts the job immediately.

Alternatively, use **`POST /api/v1/slice/prepared`** when the 3MF already embeds print settings from a previous OrcaSlicer session — no profile resolution is needed.

## Packing / arrangement

Use **`POST /api/v1/pack`** to distribute STL geometry across build plates before slicing. Three modes: supply a template `.3mf`, profile UUIDs (preferred — catalog-aware), or explicit bed dimensions. The packed `.3mf` is returned directly (synchronous, up to 120 s).

## Error conventions

- **422** — caller-side validation failure (bad UUIDs, missing required fields, etc.).
- **503** — Laminus is not yet ready; the catalog is still building. Retry after `GET /api/v1/health` reports `catalog_loaded: true`.
- **400 / 408 / 500** — OrcaSlicer-side failures; check server logs for details.

post.summary: Get merged project_settings.config for a profile set
post.description:
Resolves the full inheritance chains for the given machine, process, and filament UUIDs and returns the merged `project_settings.config` dict — exactly what would be embedded inside a `.3mf` before slicing.

**Primary use cases:**
- Inspect resolved print settings (temperatures, speeds, gcode) before committing to a slice job.
- Allow Themis to diff embedded settings against a chosen preset to warn the user of overrides (`POST /api/v1/jobs/check-overrides`).
- Verify that `layer_gcode` is populated (see OrcaSlicer -51 error) before slicing.

The response is the raw merged dict with inheritance stripped — keys like `inherits`, `compatible_printers`, `is_custom_defined`, and `from` are removed. Multi-filament keys are returned as arrays (one value per slot).

Returns **503** while the catalog is initialising.

422.description: UUID not found in catalog, wrong type (e.g. process UUID used where machine expected), or filament_uuids is empty

503.description: Catalog not yet ready — retry after /api/v1/health reports catalog_loaded: true

get.summary: List profiles excluded from the catalog
get.description:
Profiles dropped by the last catalog build, each with the reason. An unresolvable `inherits` parent here is the signal that an OrcaSlicer update renamed or removed a vendor base that a user profile was building on.

Must be registered before `/api/v1/profiles/{profile_uuid}` — Starlette matches path routes in registration order, and `{profile_uuid}` would otherwise swallow this path as a literal UUID lookup and always 404.

Returns **503** while the catalog is still building.

post.summary: Suggest machine presets for a printer model
post.description:
Candidate machine presets for (manufacturer, model), best first. Empty `candidates` (not 404) when nothing matches. `match_reason`: `exact_model`, `fuzzy_name`, `vendor_only` (same vendor, different model; low confidence, capped).

Every response carries `catalog_version` (also as `X-Catalog-Version`); `stale: true` when served from a cached catalog while a fresh one is pending.

503.description: No catalog, live or cached: error code `catalog_unavailable`

post.summary: List nozzle variants of a printer model
post.description: Machine presets that are nozzle variants of the best-matching model, ordered by diameter then flow. Exactly one has `is_default_guess` (0.4 standard if present, else the smallest standard variant). Empty `variants` when the model is unknown.

503.description: No catalog, live or cached: error code `catalog_unavailable`

get.summary: Process/filament presets compatible with a machine
get.description: Presets whose resolved `compatible_printers` is empty or names this machine. `kind=process|filament` narrows; default both. `compatible_models` is omitted for universal presets. 404 `{"error": "unknown_machine_ref"}`, 422 `{"error": "invalid_kind"}`.

503.description: No catalog, live or cached: error code `catalog_unavailable`

get.summary: Can this machine ref (and bed) be sliced for?
get.description: Always 200. `supported` is false with `reason` `unknown_machine_ref` or `bed_mismatch` (`bed_x`/`bed_y` in mm, 1 mm tolerance; a machine with no declared bed size is never ruled out). `reason` is null when supported.

503.description: No catalog, live or cached: error code `catalog_unavailable`

post.description:
Accepts a `.3mf` that already contains `Metadata/project_settings.config` (e.g., exported from OrcaSlicer desktop or produced by `POST /api/v1/jobs` with `export_3mf` set). No catalog lookup or profile merging is performed — OrcaSlicer uses the embedded settings verbatim.

Use this endpoint when you already have a fully-configured 3MF and want to avoid the overhead of profile resolution. Typical callers: Themis queue engine dispatching pre-packed project 3MFs, or debugging with a known-good 3MF from the desktop app.

**Geometry-only retry** works the same as in `POST /api/v1/jobs`: when `geometry_only_retry=true` (default) and the first slice fails, the API retries with `Metadata/model_settings.config` stripped from the 3MF.

**`export_3mf`:** when set, OrcaSlicer embeds the sliced GCode into a `.3mf` and the download endpoint returns that file instead of a standalone `.gcode`.

The response and job lifecycle are identical to `POST /api/v1/jobs`.

400.description: Bad filename (null bytes, semicolons, or missing Content-Disposition filename)

422.description: File is not a .3mf, or plate < 1

503.description: Too many concurrent slice jobs — retry when a slot opens (check active_jobs in GET /api/v1/health)

post.description:
Runs OrcaSlicer with `--arrange 0 --export-3mf` to render a plate thumbnail PNG without disturbing the model's geometry or generating GCode. Returns the PNG bytes directly with `Content-Type: image/png`.

**Blocking:** waits up to 120 seconds for OrcaSlicer to finish. No job tracking — this is fire-and-forget from the caller's perspective.

The endpoint accepts only `.3mf` files. The 3MF must embed a valid plate (the requested `plate` number must exist in the model). OrcaSlicer writes the PNG to `Metadata/plate_{N}.png` inside the output 3MF; the endpoint extracts and returns that PNG, cleaning up all temporary files afterwards.

All error conditions (OrcaSlicer failure, timeout, missing PNG output) return **422** with a JSON detail object `{"error": "..."}` describing the cause.

422.description: OrcaSlicer returned non-zero, no PNG found in output, plate < 1, bad filename, or non-.3mf file uploaded. Also returned on timeout (the OrcaSlicer process is killed).

post.summary: Pack N STLs onto as many plates as needed (synchronous)
post.description:
Distributes STL geometry across build plates via OrcaSlicer `--arrange 1 --orient 1`. Returns the resulting multi-plate `.3mf` directly as `application/octet-stream`. **Blocks for up to 120 seconds.**

## Bed / settings source (mutually exclusive — supply exactly one)

**1. Template file** (`template` field)
Upload a `.3mf` whose `Metadata/project_settings.config` carries the printer and bed configuration. OrcaSlicer reads bed dimensions and settings from that config. Use this when you already have a known-good 3MF template from a previous session.

**2. Profile UUIDs** (`machine_uuid` + `process_uuid` + `filament_uuids`)
The container resolves profiles from its catalog, builds the settings internally, and constructs a minimal bed-only template (only `printable_area` and `printable_height` are embedded — no full machine config that could override the bed size). Templates for a given UUID combination are cached in memory, so repeated calls with the same profiles are fast. This mode requires `catalog_loaded: true`.

**3. Explicit bed dimensions** (`bed_x` + `bed_y` + `bed_z`, all in mm)
Laminus constructs a minimal bed template from the supplied dimensions. `bed_z` is the printable height (not the physical Z travel). No profile catalog or template file needed — useful when you want geometry-only packing without print settings.

## STL inputs

- `files` — one or more `.stl` files (max 50 per request)
- Filenames must not contain null bytes, newlines, or semicolons
- Duplicate filenames in the same batch are deduplicated with a numeric suffix

## Notes

- OrcaSlicer auto-orients objects (`--orient 1`) to minimise support material. Pass orient=false to skip (not yet exposed as a parameter — file a request).
- The packed `.3mf` preserves `Metadata/project_settings.config` from the template but discards any geometry or model_settings from it.
- All temporary files are cleaned up after the response is sent.

400.description: Bad filename in STL or template upload, OrcaSlicer arrange process failed (non-zero exit or missing output file), or failed to build the combined 3MF

408.description: Pack operation timed out after 120 seconds

422.description: No STL files provided, more than 50 STLs, non-.stl file in files list, non-.3mf template, bed dimensions ≤ 0, invalid filament_uuids JSON, UUID not found in catalog, or no settings source provided

500.description: Unexpected system error — check server logs

503.description: Profile catalog not yet ready (UUID mode only)

post.summary: Auto-arrange and orient objects in a 3MF (synchronous)
post.description:
Runs OrcaSlicer's plate-packing (`--arrange 1`) and auto-orientation (`--orient 1`) on an existing `.3mf` and returns the rearranged `.3mf` directly as `application/octet-stream`.

**Blocking:** waits up to `ARRANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 120 s) for OrcaSlicer to finish. No job tracking — call completes synchronously.

**When to use this vs `POST /api/v1/pack`:**
- Use `POST /api/v1/arrange` when you already have a `.3mf` with the correct geometry and want to repack it (e.g., after hand-editing or re-importing).
- Use `POST /api/v1/pack` when starting from STL files that need to be combined into a 3MF first.

**Settings preservation:** the input 3MF's `Metadata/project_settings.config` is passed to OrcaSlicer via `--datadir`, which means OrcaSlicer may load its own machine profiles from the user presets under `/config` (symlinked into Orca's datadir — see `ORCA_DATADIR`). The `Metadata/model_settings.config` (extruder/slot assignments) from the input 3MF is preserved in the output.

All temporary files are cleaned up after the response is sent, including the stable output copy used to serve the download.

400.description: Bad filename (null bytes, semicolons, or missing Content-Disposition filename), non-.3mf file uploaded, OrcaSlicer returned non-zero exit code, or output file missing after OrcaSlicer claims success

408.description: OrcaSlicer arrange timed out — reduce model complexity or increase ARRANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

500.description: Unexpected system error — check server logs

post.summary: List the objects in an OrcaSlicer/Bambu .3mf
post.description: Returns each object's `id`, `name`, extruder, per-object override keys, part subtypes (e.g. `modifier_part`) and current instance count. Use the names/ids in `POST /api/v1/projects/subset`. Names are not unique in a project; ids are.

post.summary: List a .3mf's objects with plate names and a preview image of each object
post.description:
For each object: `id`, `name`, `extruder`, `plates` (`[{plate, name, instances}]` - `name` is the plate's name in the project, or `Plate N` when unnamed) and `preview`.

`preview` is a rendering of **the object itself** (not the plate): a 3/4-view PNG, transparent background, tinted with the object's filament colour, modifier/negative parts omitted; `{mime, width, height, data_base64}`, or `null` when the object has nothing printable. Use the `id`s with `/api/v1/projects/subset` or `/api/v1/projects/merge`.

`size` is the square image edge in px (32-1024, default 256). Set `images=false` for names/plates only (fast). Rendering is CPU-bound: roughly 0.5 s per object for typical models, so a 20-object project takes ~10 s.

post.summary: Keep only chosen objects (x quantity) from a .3mf and arrange them on the fewest plates
post.description:
Takes a `.3mf`, a `selection` (JSON list of `{"name"|"id"|"plate": ..., "qty": n}`; `plate` selects everything on that source plate) and optionally a `machine_uuid`, and returns a `.3mf` containing only those objects, `qty` copies each, arranged by OrcaSlicer across as many plates as needed.

**Preservation:** the returned file is the source project with only the chosen objects kept; meshes and `model_settings.config` are copied byte-for-byte, so per-object/per-part overrides, modifier parts, height-range modifiers and painted data (colour, supports, seam, fuzzy skin) survive. OrcaSlicer is used only to compute the layout (plate membership + instance transforms), which is written into that file; OrcaSlicer's own re-export is not returned because it splits cross-plate instances into clone objects that lose name/overrides/extruder.

**Printer:** when `machine_uuid` is given, the bed/printer keys of the project are replaced from that machine preset and the embedded process preset's printer-compatibility list is cleared. Process/filament settings are otherwise left as in the source project.

**Plates:** OrcaSlicer's multi-plate arrange is used as-is; response header `X-Plate-Count` reports the result; `X-Warnings` lists any object not resting on the bed (empty when fine). Selector names matching several objects are rejected (422) — use `id`.

Blocking; limited by `ARRANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

422.description: Bad selection, unknown/ambiguous object, unknown machine_uuid

503.description: machine_uuid given but catalog not ready

post.summary: Combine selections from several .3mf files into one .3mf, arranged on the fewest plates
post.description:
Upload several `.3mf` files as repeated `files` parts and a `selection` JSON list whose entries each name their source with `file` (the uploaded filename, or the 0-based upload index) plus one of `id` / `name` / `plate` and a `qty`:

`[{"file": "hex.3mf", "plate": 1, "qty": 2}, {"file": 1, "id": 8, "qty": 1}]`

`plate` selects every object on that plate of the source (x its count there x `qty`). Returns one `.3mf`. Per-object/part overrides, modifiers and painted data travel with each object. **Project-wide settings (process, filament, printer, thumbnails) come from the first uploaded file** (the base); differences in the other sources are listed in the `X-Merge-Warnings` header, which also reports any object that ends up not resting on the bed (floating/sunk). A non-base object using a filament slot the base does not have is rejected (422). `machine_uuid` retargets the bed/printer as in `/api/v1/projects/subset`.

Headers: `X-Plate-Count`, `X-Instance-Count`, `X-Merge-Warnings`. Blocking; limited by `ARRANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

422.description: Bad selection, unknown/ambiguous object, unknown file, unknown machine_uuid, incompatible sources

503.description: machine_uuid given but catalog not ready

post.description:
Upload a flat OrcaSlicer preset JSON into the user config volume at `/config/user/default/{type}/`. A catalog rebuild is triggered in the background automatically — wait ~5 s and call `GET /api/v1/profiles` to confirm the profile appears before using it in a slice job.

**Requirements for the JSON file:**
- Must have a `.json` extension
- `type` must be exactly `machine`, `process`, or `filament`

**Prefer a thin preset over a flattened one.** Declare `inherits` naming the vendor base plus only the keys you are actually changing. Inheritance is resolved against the profile tree as it exists at slice time, so an OrcaSlicer update that improves the vendor base rolls straight through into your profile. A fully-flattened preset (no `inherits`) is frozen at the version it was flattened from and silently misses every later vendor fix — use it only when you want a permanent fork.

If the base is renamed or removed by a later OrcaSlicer release the profile is dropped from the catalog rather than served half-resolved; `GET /api/v1/profiles/broken` reports it.

**Profile persistence:** the uploaded file is written to a Docker volume (`/config/user/`). It survives container restarts but is not baked into the image. Re-upload after replacing the container with a clean image.

**UUID stability:** user profiles receive a UUID derived from `(user, rel_path)` so the UUID changes if the file is renamed or moved.

400.description: Invalid `type` (must be machine, process, or filament), bad filename (null bytes, semicolons, path traversal), or file does not have a .json extension

post.summary: Rescan profiles and rebuild the catalog
post.description:
Re-walks the system and user profile trees, re-verifies every `inherits` chain, and rebuilds the catalog dictionary.

The catalog is normally rebuilt automatically — the cache key covers the OrcaSlicer version, the vendor profile bundles, and every file under `/config/user/`, so any preset change voids it. Use this endpoint to force the work anyway: after editing profiles in place on a bind mount, or to re-check which profiles are broken after an OrcaSlicer upgrade.

Returns immediately; the rebuild runs in the background. Poll `GET /api/v1/health` until `catalog_building` is `false`, then call `GET /api/v1/profiles/broken` for profiles whose inheritance no longer resolves.

get.description:
Returns service readiness information. **Always call this first** — profile and slice endpoints return **503** while `catalog_loading` is `true`.

**Response fields:**
- `status` — always `"healthy"` when the process is running
- `orcaslicer_installed` — whether the OrcaSlicer binary exists at `/usr/local/bin/orcaslicer`
- `orcaslicer_version` — version string from `orcaslicer --version`, or `null` if the binary is not installed or timed out
- `orca_version` — installed OrcaSlicer release (e.g. `"2.4.2"`), read from the install's `.version` marker, falling back to the `ORCA_VERSION` env var; `null` if neither is available
- `config_mounted` — whether `/config` exists (volume mount check)
- `system_profiles_available` — whether the OrcaSlicer AppImage's profiles directory is present (required for catalog build)
- `catalog_loaded` — `true` when the profile catalog is fully built and ready; `false` during initial startup or rebuild
- `catalog_building` — `true` while a catalog rebuild is in progress
- `catalog_profile_count` — `{machine: N, process: N, filament: N}` when loaded, otherwise `null`
- `catalog_skipped_count` — number of profiles excluded from the catalog on the last build (unresolvable `inherits` parent, unparseable JSON, etc.) — call `GET /api/v1/profiles/broken` for which profiles and why; `null` if not yet built
- `active_jobs` — number of jobs currently in `slicing` status

post.summary: Remove stale temp files from failed/interrupted jobs
post.description:
Scans `/tmp/jobs` and `/tmp/arrange` for leftover directories/files not accounted for by any currently active job, and removes the ones older than `min_age_seconds`. This catches clutter that the normal job-eviction sweep can't see — e.g. scratch dirs from an `/api/v1/arrange`, `/api/v1/pack`, or `/api/v1/slice/thumbnail` request that never finished because the container was killed mid-request, or `/tmp/jobs` entries left behind by a slice job that existed before a restart.

**`dry_run=true`** reports what would be removed (path count + total bytes) without deleting anything — use this to preview before committing.

**`min_age_seconds`** (default 300) guards against deleting a directory that's still being written to by an in-flight request; pass `0` to remove everything unowned regardless of age.

get.description: Version, engine, readiness, feature flags and limits. Clients should feature-detect from `features` rather than parsing versions.

post.description: Upload a model plus profile UUIDs to start a slice. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe: the same key with the same body returns the original job (`Idempotent-Replay: true`); the same key with a different body is a 422 `idempotency_key_reuse`; a key whose first request is still being processed is a 409. Keys are remembered for 24 h, in memory (not across restarts).

409.description: Idempotency key in use by an in-flight request

422.description: Validation error or idempotency key reuse

503.description: Catalog not ready or too many active jobs

get.description: Typed server-sent events with sequential `id`s: `log` ({message}), `dropped` ({message}), and one terminal `completed` or `failed` ({reason}). Send `Last-Event-ID` to skip events already seen (the buffer is replayed from the start on every connect).

404.description: Unknown job, or job data lost in a restart

get.description: One-time download: the job's files are deleted afterwards (its record stays listed with `artifact.available: false`).
Flat list across machine/process/filament presets. `manufacturer`, `model` and `nozzle` must be given together (compatibility filter).

process_uuid.title: Process Uuid
process_uuid.description: Override the project's process preset (requires machine_uuid)

filament_uuids.title: Filament Uuids
filament_uuids.description: JSON array of filament preset UUIDs, one per slot (requires machine_uuid)

process_uuid.title: Process Uuid
process_uuid.description: Override the project's process preset (requires machine_uuid)

filament_uuids.title: Filament Uuids
filament_uuids.description: JSON array of filament preset UUIDs, one per slot (requires machine_uuid)

extra_config.title: Extra Config
extra_config.description: JSON object merged into project settings

bed_x.title: Bed X
bed_x.description: Bed X dimension in mm (alternative to template / UUIDs)

bed_z.title: Bed Z
bed_z.description: Bed Z printable height in mm

machine_uuid.title: Machine Uuid
machine_uuid.description: Stable UUID of the machine (printer) profile. Obtain from `GET /api/v1/profiles` or `GET /api/v1/profiles/{uuid}`. Machine UUIDs are derived from the (manufacturer, model, nozzle) tuple and are stable across catalog rebuilds.

process_uuid.title: Process Uuid
process_uuid.description: Stable UUID of the process (print quality) profile, e.g. `0.20mm Standard`. Must be compatible with the supplied machine — check `compatible_printers` in the profile detail.

filament_uuids.title: Filament Uuids
filament_uuids.description: List of filament profile UUIDs, one per extruder slot in slot order (slot 1 first). Must be compatible with the machine. Single-extruder printers need exactly one entry.

manufacturer.title: Manufacturer
manufacturer.description: Printer manufacturer display name, e.g. 'Bambu Lab'.

model_key.title: Model Key
model_key.description: Caller's own model key; matched alongside `model`.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Service readiness and version information. Always check `/api/v1/health` first — profile and slice endpoints return **503** while `catalog_loading` is `true`.

tags.name: profiles
tags.description: Machine, process, and filament preset catalog derived from the OrcaSlicer AppImage's bundled profiles plus any user-uploaded profiles in `/config/user/`. Profiles are identified by stable UUIDs derived from their (manufacturer, model, nozzle) tuple (machine) or (source, rel_path) (process/filament), so UUIDs remain constant across catalog rebuilds as long as the profile files don't move.

tags.name: slice
tags.description: Asynchronous slice job lifecycle: **start → poll → download**. Jobs are kept in memory and evicted after download or after `JOB_TTL_SECONDS` (default 3600). A maximum of `MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` (default 4) jobs may slice simultaneously; additional requests receive **503** until a slot opens.

tags.name: arrange
tags.description: Synchronous plate arrangement and STL packing. No job tracking — responses block until OrcaSlicer finishes (up to `ARRANGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 120). Use `POST /api/v1/pack` to combine multiple STLs into a single multi-plate `.3mf`, and `POST /api/v1/arrange` to re-pack an existing `.3mf`.

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Job history across the lifetime of the container — every slice job ever created, including ones already evicted from the active `jobs` table. Backs the Web UI's status/history view.

tags.name: maintenance
tags.description: On-demand disk cleanup for temp files left behind by failed or interrupted slice/arrange/pack runs (e.g., after a container crash mid-request).
